surface: Reading mode through the same grid without frozen panes, the control for the frozen traversal: every body cell read once, in row-major order.

steps.note: From the control before the grid, the reading cursor moves on to the grid, which a reader announces by its role.

unsupported.nvda: NVDA has no interaction level: browse mode reads into a table without entering it, so there is nothing to enter.

steps.note: VoiceOver interacts with the grid (VO-Shift-Down), the way its user reads a table cell by cell.

Each read moves one item on: NVDA reads one line of its browse-mode buffer (a cell with its row, column and the headers that changed), VoiceOver one cell of the row it is in, wrapping to the next row and on out of the table. The reads are sized for both readers to reach the control after the grid, the overlay clones included. On the grid page the headers are named, so a header letter never stands beside a row number and reads as a cell reference NVDA spells A 1. Finding (known, the overlay clones): after the body every reader reads the header row and the row headers a second time, from the overlay clones, and NVDA and VoiceOver with Chromium count the clones' rows in the table's size (`9 rows` for a grid of 4). The traversal's items are the body cells, so it does not count those copies: this control proves the body is read once and in order, not that the whole grid is.

The last read announces the control after the grid, the page's last item, which both readers repeat once they reach it: the reads before it covered the whole grid, the overlay clones included. VoiceOver reads on out of the table it interacted with, so no read leaves it.
